subject: Request: regional availability cushion & graduated monthly credit trigger
messages:
From: Sam Kelly <sam.kelly@tidaltech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elinor Shaw <ops@tidaltech.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification on regional uptime splits and monthly credit triggers

Marissa —

Thanks for the draft SLA. A couple of items came up from our platform and procurement teams that we'd like to get clarified before we move to legal redlines:

- TidalTech runs bursty batched inference in eu-west and needs a small operational tolerance for scheduled maintenance and cold-starts during heavy batch windows. Can Redwood provide a narrow "alpha cushion" for the EU region (we're proposing 0.5% per month) rather than a global change?
- We also want credits to be triggered in a graduated way instead of an all-or-nothing monthly cap: small monthly credits for minor drops (e.g., 99.6-99.8), larger credits for deeper outages. Can you propose a concrete schedule?
- Finally, we need a carve-in for planned cross-region failovers (30–90 minutes) so we aren’t double-credited for transient failovers during a controlled migration.

I attached the list of questions procurement compiled (TidalTech-SLA-questions.xlsx). Can your team propose specific language we can run with legal? We're targeting a pilot go-live in early July.

Best,
Sam
Sam Kelly
VP Platform, TidalTech
[Attachment: TidalTech-SLA-questions.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Kelly <sam.kelly@tidaltech.com>
Cc: Elinor Shaw <ops@tidaltech.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on regional uptime splits and monthly credit triggers

Sam —

Thanks, this is helpful and clear. Short answer: yes — we can propose a regional "alpha cushion" for EU-hosted workloads and a graduated monthly credit schedule. I'll outline a specific proposal below and attach a redline for your review. High-level summary:

1) Regional alpha cushion (EU only for pilot)
   - 99.95% baseline availability for EU region for production endpoints.
   - For the pilot (first 3 months), a 0.5% operational cushion applies to EU production traffic for batched inference workloads only. This means remedial credits are calculated against 99.45% (99.95 - 0.5) for triggers only — not for long-term SLA baselining.

2) Graduated monthly credit trigger (example bands)
   - 99.9% — no credit
   - 99.6%–99.9% — 5% of monthly invoice credited
   - 99.0%–99.6% — 15% credit
   - <99.0% — 40% credit, capped at two months' invoice (to limit tail risk)

3) Controlled failover carve-in
   - Planned cross-region failovers (announced >72 hours) and automated regional failovers in Cross-Region DR drills (<=90 minutes) are excluded from credit triggers when executed per runbook and with prior notice.

4) Measurement and telemetry
   - Availability measured at the per-route token-serving level, aggregated to region-month. We will share a monthly availability report and provide raw request/response logs under NDA for the pilot period.

Next steps: I've attached a redline that inserts the wording above into the SLA and an example credit schedule. If that looks good, I can circulate to ops for final input and then send a PDF for procurement/legal. Happy to jump on a 30m call next week to walk Sam and Elinor through the mechanics.

Attached: Redwood-proposal-alpha-cushion-redline.docx

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-proposal-alpha-cushion-redline.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on regional uptime splits and monthly credit triggers

Marissa / Laura —

Quick internal notes from ops and pricing:

- Ops: The 0.5% EU alpha cushion for batched inference seems reasonable for a 3-month pilot, but we want to bind it to specific operational constraints: must be limited to routes flagged as "batch" in the route config, and we need telemetry tags from TidalTech indicating burst windows for correlation.
- Pricing: Graduated credit bands are fine but request we keep the cap to 30% of monthly invoice for standard accounts; we can make an exception to 2 months' invoice for strategic pilots, but need approval from finance.

Action items:
- Marissa: update the redline to indicate route-level flagging and telemetry contract (we use a simple JSON tag schema).
- Priyom: can you confirm whether the runtime can honor per-route "batch" labels at serving time and whether we can generate a monthly route-level availability CSV for TidalTech?

I'll be on a call with finance Monday — if we want the expanded cap for the pilot we should sync before then.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Kelly <sam.kelly@tidaltech.com>
Cc: Elinor Shaw <ops@tidaltech.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on regional uptime splits and monthly credit triggers

Sam / Elinor —

Following internal alignment, attached is an updated PDF with our proposed redlines (TidalTech-SLA-redlines-20270516.pdf). Summary of the final changes we can accept for the pilot:

- EU regional pilot: 99.95% baseline with 0.5% operational cushion applying only to per-route flagged "batch" workloads for the first 90 days post-go-live.
- Credit bands adjusted: 5% (99.6–99.9), 15% (99.0–99.6), 30% (<99.0) with pilot exception to allow up to 60% cap (equivalent to two months' invoice) subject to finance sign-off.
- Controlled failover carve-in: Planned cross-region failovers (72h notice) and automated failovers <=90 minutes follow runbook exclusion; transient failovers beyond 90 minutes are eligible for credits.
- Telemetry: Redwood will tag route traffic with a JSON "batch" flag and provide a per-route availability CSV monthly. Access to raw logs available under NDA.

If this aligns with TidalTech's needs, I'll get legal to prepare an amendment and send a DocuSign link to the procurement contact. Proposed pilot go-live window: 2027-07-05 to 2027-10-02.

Thanks — happy to walk through the PDF in a 30-minute session if you'd like.

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: TidalTech-SLA-redlines-20270516.pdf (pdf)]
